title_en: The man who came from the farthest part of the city
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The man from the farthest part of the city

claims.statement_en: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said, my people, follow the messengers.
He told them to follow those who ask them for no payment and who are rightly guided.

He asked why he should not worship the One who created him and to whom they will be returned, and asked whether he should take gods besides Him, when, if the Merciful wished him harm, their intercession would not avail him at all and they could not rescue him, for then he would be in clear error.
He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him.
He was told to enter the Garden, and he said that he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him and made him among the honoured.

chapters.summary_md: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and told his people to follow the messengers [c1]. He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden, and he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him [c5].
chapters.body_md: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said, my people, follow the messengers [c1]. He told them to follow those who ask them for no payment and who are rightly guided [c2]. He asked why he should not worship the One who created him and to whom they will be returned, and asked whether he should take gods besides Him, when, if the Merciful wished him harm, their intercession would not avail him at all and they could not rescue him, for then he would be in clear error [c3]. He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden, and he said that he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him and made him among the honoured [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat do not name the man, the city or the messengers [c1]. The ayah says that he was told to enter the Garden and does not say how or when he came to be there [c5].
chapters.kids_md: A man came running from the farthest part of the city [c1]. He told his people to follow the messengers [c1]. He said that he believed in their Lord [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the man argues from his own worship of the One who created him [c3]. Another is that the passage ends with his wish that his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the man's name, his age or his work.
- Not established: the name of the city, or who the messengers were; the ayat before this passage speak of them.
- Not established: how he came to be told to enter the Garden, or what his people did.
- Not established: whether he is related to any other man described with similar words in another passage; nothing in the ayat links them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: he is called Habib, and the city is identified in later works.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man is called Habib, and later works give his trade, the name of the city and the manner of his death.
Hadith to add later: reports about the man of the city, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
